It is shipped as printed rather than silently corrected, and flagged in public_note. RIGHTS: checked, no reserved right locatable and therefore no block. Clean pass, with two things recorded. STEP 3b (instrument identity): the table is built from the SPSS file's q12_1..q12_8 block, whose variable labels read 'Zufriedenheit <domain>' across the 8 domains Freunde/Bekannte, Freizeitgestaltung/Hobbys, Gesundheit, Einkommen/finanzielle Sicherheit, Beruf/Arbeit, Wohnsituation, Familienleben/Kinder, Partnerschaft/Sexualitaet -- so 'domain_satisfaction' is the right name and there is no mismatch with the live data. What the S1 File calls 'Fragebogen zur Lebenszufriedenheit (FLZ)' is in fact the FLZ^M (Fragen zur Lebenszufriedenheit-Module; Henrich & Herschbach, EJPA 2000, 16(3):150-159), whose General Life Satisfaction module is exactly these 8 domains rated twice -- once for importance (q11, the sibling table reinwarth_2023_domain_importance) and once for satisfaction (q12, this table) -- with a weighted importance x satisfaction composite (q13, labelled 'FLZ-<domain>', range -12..+20, not shipped). It is NOT Fahrenberg/Myrtek/Schumacher/Braehler's FLZ sold by Testzentrale, which is 10 domains x 7 items on a 7-point scale. The shipped 'instrument' field names both the paper's label and the FLZ^M. MAPPING (data_labels, derivation pattern 1 = exempt): data/reinwarth_2023_domains_wellbeing.py melts value_vars=[f'q12_{i}' for i in 1..8] with var_name='item', so the IRW item code IS the .sav column name; nothing is positional and nothing is renamed. The .sav variable labels tie each code to its domain, and S1 File Table 8 prints the same 8 domains in the same order on the administered form -- a string match, not an order inference. Value labels 1=Unzufrieden, 2=Eher unzufrieden, 3=Eher zufrieden, 4=Ziemlich zufrieden, 5=Sehr zufrieden are identical for all 8 columns and match the live resp set {1,2,3,4,5} exactly; the -1 'Keine Angabe' sentinel is dropped by the script and is absent from the live data, so no row is emitted for it. WORDING: item_text and option_text are transcribed verbatim from S1 File Table 8 (the German form as administered); item_text is a bare domain label because that is literally what the form prints under the shared stem 'Wie zufrieden sind Sie...', which is shipped in 'instructions' together with the two preceding instruction sentences. No stems were invented and nothing was expanded. English is the study's own 'authorized English version ... provided as a courtesy to readers' from S1 File Table 9 (translation_source=study_supplied); note its level-1 anchor reads 'Not at all satisfied' where the German is the plain 'Unzufrieden' -- that is the authors' rendering, transcribed as given rather than corrected. RIGHTS: no reserved right could be located or quoted for the FLZ^M. The originating publication (Henrich & Herschbach 2000, EJPA) carries only Hogrefe & Huber's article copyright notice -- a notice about the article, not a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case) -- and the only distribution-related sentence in it is 'the FLZM modules have been made available to many colleagues for use in their own studies, with the proviso that the test authors be allowed to use the raw data for the psychometric evaluation of the instrument and as comparative data', which is a condition on data sharing by administering researchers, not a fee, permission-to-redistribute, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause. No rights-holder page stating terms was reachable: assessment-info.de (vid=54) returned ECONNREFUSED on two attempts, and the authors' TUM contact is an order address rather than a terms page. Silence is permission, so this extracts normally; instrument_rights_register.csv has no FLZ/FLZ^M row and none was written (a round may write block rows only). FLAGGED FOR THE HUMAN: the FLZ^M is obtained by request from Henrich/Herschbach at TU Munich rather than downloaded, which is the shape that would attract the 2026-09-05 'any stated use restriction' ruling if a quotable statement of terms ever turns up; the wording shipped here nevertheless comes from this study's own CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit, which published all 8 domains itself.
